This memorandum summarizes the terms and considerations associated with the renewal of the vendor services agreement between Halbrook Logistics Group and Corestone Supply Partners, effective for the twelve-month period beginning March 1 and concluding the last day of February of the following year. The purpose of this document is to provide an overview of the renewal discussion, the changes to pricing and service levels since the prior agreement, and the internal approvals required before the contract can be executed by both parties.

Corestone Supply Partners has served as Halbrook Logistics Group's primary vendor for warehouse packaging materials, palletizing equipment maintenance, and related consumable supplies since the initial agreement was signed three years ago. Over that period, the relationship has been managed on the Halbrook side by Denise Okafor, Director of Procurement, with day-to-day coordination handled by Marcus Feldt in the Operations department. On the Corestone side, the primary point of contact has been Rebecca Linden, Senior Account Manager, supported by Tom Grissom in Corestone's logistics coordination team. Both parties have expressed general satisfaction with the working relationship, and no material disputes or service failures were recorded during the most recent contract term, aside from a minor delay in Q3 shipment of stretch wrap film, which was resolved within the contractually allowed window and did not result in any penalty assessment.

As part of the renewal negotiation, Corestone proposed a 3.2 percent increase in unit pricing across the standard packaging materials category, citing increased costs of raw resin inputs and elevated freight surcharges affecting their own supply chain. Halbrook's procurement team reviewed this request against current market benchmarks obtained from two comparable vendors, Ashgrove Packaging Solutions and Deniston Industrial Supply, and determined that the proposed increase was within a reasonable range, falling slightly below the average increase reported by competitors during the same period. After a brief round of negotiation, Corestone agreed to cap the increase at 2.75 percent for the first six months of the renewed term, with the remaining 0.45 percent taking effect at the midpoint of the contract, contingent on no significant volatility in resin pricing during that window. This staged approach was proposed by Rebecca Linden as a way to ease the transition for Halbrook's budgeting cycle, and Denise Okafor confirmed that this structure aligns with the finance department's preference for predictable quarterly cost adjustments.

In addition to pricing, the renewal includes several updates to the service level agreement. The standard delivery window for routine orders has been reduced from five business days to four business days, a change requested by Halbrook's operations team following feedback from the Dallas and Reno distribution centers regarding inventory turnover constraints. Corestone has agreed to this adjustment without additional charge, noting that recent investments in their regional distribution hub in Oklahoma City have created sufficient capacity to support the shortened window without disrupting service to their other clients. The renewal also formalizes a quarterly business review meeting, to be held via video conference, during which both parties will review fill rates, on-time delivery percentages, and any emerging supply chain risks. This formal review process was not part of the original agreement and represents an enhancement suggested by Marcus Feldt after an internal audit recommended more structured vendor oversight across all major supply relationships.

The renewal agreement also addresses the equipment maintenance component of the contract, specifically the quarterly servicing of the automated palletizing units at the Reno facility. Corestone will continue to provide this service under the existing terms, with technician visits scheduled for the second week of each quarter. Halbrook's facilities team has requested that Corestone provide advance notice of at least ten business days prior to each scheduled visit, an adjustment from the previous seven-day notice requirement, to allow for better coordination with the facility's production schedule. Corestone has accepted this change without objection.

From a contractual standponing, the renewal document retains the same termination clause structure as the prior agreement, allowing either party to terminate with ninety days written notice, and it preserves the existing confidentiality and data handling provisions related to shared inventory forecasts and order history. Legal review of the renewal draft was completed by Halbrook's internal counsel, Priya Nandakumar, who confirmed that no substantive changes to liability or indemnification language were introduced in this renewal cycle. Corestone's legal team similarly confirmed no objections to the retained language during their review.

Before the renewal can be finalized, the agreement requires sign-off from Halbrook's Vice President of Operations, Gregory Ashcombe, as well as confirmation from the finance department that the revised pricing structure has been incorporated into the upcoming fiscal year budget projections. Denise Okafor has indicated that she expects to have both approvals in hand within the next two weeks, at which point the finalized agreement will be routed to Corestone for countersignature. Assuming no delays in this process, the renewed contract is expected to be fully executed before the current agreement's expiration date, ensuring continuity of service without any gap in coverage for packaging materials or scheduled equipment maintenance.
